individually_inspected_images.observation: The lowered body remains one readable crescent, with a continuous crest and visibly open inner bay. The original steep sail-like elevation is reduced; tips remain separated and unequal. The unchanged high camera target makes the body appear lower in frame, not artificially enlarged.
The outer body remains broad and continuous, with the two ends tapering into the same body. No detached horns, extra hump or tube-like limb appears.
A single low convex upper profile returns to the same ground line at both ends. No vertical skirt or added base is visible.
One crest separates a longer gradual stoss run from the shorter, steeper lee descent. The body is low, but not reduced to a flat plate.
One low continuous central mass with ground-level tips. No secondary peak is visible.
The broad outer arc and concave inner opening read clearly as a crescent; unequal horn endpoints remain. The crest separates broad stoss and narrower lee bands. No closed ring or filled mouth.
The crest and lee/stoss shape hierarchy remain legible without sand color. The body is coherent and not dependent on painted or textured shadow.
The outer sweep, two ends and open inner bay remain readable at the locked hero angle. No added appendage or closed ring.
The closed underside follows the same concave crescent; the opening has not been triangulated into a convex hull.
Height tapers continuously into a ground-level pointed tip; no stepped skirt, local lump, tubular separation or split appears.
The curved crest and lee surface converge into the second ground-level tip as one continuous mass; no detached or upright blade is visible.

locked_comparison.observation: Original and candidate retain the same footprint and framing. Peak height changes from 1.600000024 m to 0.665000021 m; reduced elevation is obvious rather than hidden by camera refitting. The main crescent identity survives.
